translation.title: Ketoprofen Plaster
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and anti-inflammation in degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, epicondylitis of the humerus (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain, and post-traumatic swelling and pain.
translation.usage: Remove the release liner from the adhesive side and apply the plaster to the affected area once a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are or have been hypersensitive or photosensitive to it, if you have or have had aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.), if you are hypersensitive to ingredients that can cause cross-hypersensitivity (tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate, oxybenzone), if you are 6 months or more pregnant, or for children under 15 years. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or if you are under a doctor's care. While using this medicine and for up to 2 weeks after use, avoid outdoor activities regardless of the weather, and when you go out, cover the application site with clothing, sunglasses, a hat, sunscreen, etc. so that it is not exposed to ultraviolet light. White or thin clothing can let ultraviolet light through, so wear colored clothing. Do not use it on the eyes or mucous membranes, or on athlete's foot or ringworm (tinea). Applying it to damaged skin or mucous membranes, or to areas with eczema or rash, may cause temporary irritation and sharp pain. Do not use it under an occlusive dressing. Adverse reactions may occur - rarely shock and anaphylactoid symptoms (hives, difficulty breathing, facial swelling and other hypersensitivity-like symptoms), dry crackles, wheezing and difficulty breathing - if these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Sometimes contact dermatitis with redness, rash, itching, blisters, oozing, irritation and swelling, dry skin, pigmentation, and photosensitivity caused by direct sunlight (ultraviolet light) may occur; if symptoms are severe, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. If your symptoms do not improve after about 1 week of use, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature away from moisture and light, and keep out of reach of children.
